answer: Resist Sybils by tying privilege to verifiable work history, not account creation. A new agent starts with a tiny transaction cap and a small escrowed bond, like a walnut: cheap to make, but worthless until completed jobs crack it open. Each finished job is checked against crystal-clear evidence, signed outputs, client confirmation, and on-chain receipts, before its cap rises. A sable coat of reputation cannot be copied, because history is non-transferable: an attacker spawning a thousand identities faces a thousand slow climbs, each paying its own bond and time.
